title: RBAC: built-in roles, custom roles, scope and inheritance

videos.script: A role in Azure is a list. It lists what a person may do, operation by operation. {{list}} Owner may do everything. Contributor may do everything except one thing: give access to others. Reader may look, and change nothing. {{four}} You will download those definitions from Microsoft's own documentation, and read them yourself. {{fetch}} Then a short program applies the rule Microsoft writes down. What a role allows, minus what it removes. {{rule}} It shows something people get wrong. Roles add up. A thing one role removes, another role can give back. {{sum}} It also shows a surprise. The Owner of a subscription cannot read a single file in it, by that route. {{data}} Last, the assignment. A role is given to a group, at a scope, and it flows down from there. {{scope}} Never up, and never sideways. Where you put an assignment decides how large a mistake can be. {{end}}
